newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: How ASC linked Booth to Macquarie's Hannes.
newsitem.headline: How ASC linked Booth to Macquarie's Hannes.

text.p: Police and Australian Securities Commission investigators used both the highest of technology and the oldest detection methods to link the fictitious Mark Booth to Macquarie Bank Ltd executive director Simon Hannes, a court was told on Tuesday.

Hannes, an executive in Macquarie's corporate advisory section, has been charged with insider trading after he allegedly bought A$2.00 TNT Ltd call options in the name of Mark Booth before the successful A$2.45 a share takeover bid for TNT by Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV (KPN).
He is also charged with trying to conceal transactions linked to the options trades which, it is alleged, made Booth/Hannes a notional profit of over A$2 million.
Hannes, an executive in Macquarie's corporate advisory division, has indicated he would plead not guilty to the transactions charges.
He has not yet responded to the insider trading charges.
Macquarie advised TNT on the takeover but Hannes was not involved with the TNT account as he was on extended leave at the time.

Police seized a Compaq laptop computer from Hannes' home in January this year and managed to restore a number of deleted files from its hard disk, the Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP) office said in documents tabled in a New South Wales court.
"Investigators discovered text files identical in terms to parts of the written communication from M. Booth to Ords (Minnett)," the DPP said.
A sheet of paper was also seized from Hannes' home which had indentations on it consisent with details of the Ord Minnett cash management account used to buy the TNT options, it said.
Police can identify what was written on the pages above using a type of pencil shading on the indented pages.
"The name M. Booth appears on a number of the documents, though only as an indentation," it said.
"It is consistent with having been written by the same hand as had written the name of the significant bank, Ord Minnett, mailbox and voicemail records."

"The fact that documents containing the indentations were found in the defendant's possession is cogent evidence supporting the inference that he was the person who, in fact, used the alias Mark Booth."
Hannes was appearing in the New South Wales local court in a committal hearing before magistrate Pat O'Shane.
The hearing adjourned for three and a half hours for her to read the two volumes of evidence submitted by the prosecution.
Indentations on pages seized from Hannes' home also had signatures for Mark Booth on the pages that were found by handwriting experts to be very similar to Hannes' own signatures.
Hannes lawyers said they have no immediate response to the documents tabled.
